messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-INC-3942 fired for api.redwood.com — high TLS handshake failures + LB target unhealthy. Severity: P1. Error spike ~2000/min. Paged: @Dana Li. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-3942

Dana Li: Acked — oncall here, looking now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Dana Li.

Alice Nguyen: On it, opening load balancer + proxy logs.

Carlos Martinez: Quick context — we cut over a canary proxy & new ALB mapping ~8–10m ago. Could be related.

Dana Li: ALB edge logs show a lot of TLS_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE and the target group health is ~60% unhealthy (502s/504s).

Alice Nguyen: First check certs: `aws acm describe-certificate --certificate-arn arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:...` cert is valid (expires 2025). Not an expiry issue.

Ben Patel: I pushed a routing/proxy config to the canary pool ~9m ago — it terminates TLS and forwards to the service.

Carlos Martinez: Looking at proxy logs — many errors like `tls: handshake failure: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and some `no suitable signature algorithm`. Seems intermediate chain missing on new proxy.

Dana Li: Ok plan: (1) rollback DNS to old ALB (low TTL 60s) to shift traffic back, (2) roll back proxy config on canary hosts, (3) re-register old targets. Which takes least time?

Alice Nguyen: DNS rollback is fastest. I'll start rollback + also begin rollback of proxy deployment in parallel.

Dana Li: Doing Route53 change to point api.redwood.com -> old-alb-12345.elb.amazonaws.com now. Command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://rollback.json --hosted-zone-id Z123`

pagerduty-bot: If not resolved in 5m, incident will escalate to SRE manager.

Eileen Park: Support seeing increased customer reports (webhooks failing, integrations). Posting initial status page note: "Partial outage impacting API TLS handshakes in some regions."

Carlos Martinez: Re-registering targets to old ALB target group: `aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0123` — done for 3/3 targets.

Ben Patel: Rolling back proxy config on canary k8s deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/proxy-canary -n infra`. Started.

Alice Nguyen: Observability: error rate trending down from ~2000/min -> ~300/min after DNS rollback started.

Dana Li: Ben — proxy rollback status?

Ben Patel: Rollback finished on 4/5 canary pods, last pod draining. Tests passing on 4/5.

Alice Nguyen: TLS handshake errors dropping to baseline in logs. No more unknown CA messages. :thumbsup:

Dana Li: Route53 propagation shows most regions at new mapping. Cloudfront/clients reporting successful TLS. Monitoring 5xxs -> baseline.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-INC-3942 marked RESOLVED by Dana Li.

Eileen Park: Status page updated: "Incident mitigated — traffic failback to stable ALB and proxy rollback. Partial customer impact cleared, some retries may be needed."

Ben Patel: Post-incident actions: missing intermediate cert during canary deploy. I'll file a follow-up: add cert-chain preflight check to CI, validate full chain on canary, and add a canary circuit breaker on ALB routing.

Dana Li: On-call handoff to @Ben Patel for follow-ups. Handoff summary: root cause — canary proxy deployed without intermediate cert chain; caused TLS handshake failures at ALB and target unhealthy. Mitigations performed — DNS rollback to old ALB, proxy rollback, re-register targets, monitor. Action items assigned to Ben.

Ben Patel: Acknowledged handoff, will take ownership of postmortem and fixes.

David Gomez: Thanks team. Please attach timelines, logs, Route53 change IDs, and the rollout IDs to the incident doc. Postmortem due within 24h.

Alice Nguyen: Adding logs/commands used and a short timeline to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/PD-INC-3942

Eileen Park: Noted — customers that opened tickets will be updated.

Dana Li: Closing thread from oncall perspective. If anything regresses, re-open PD. Great job everyone.
